html:
SMTO-FIL-0013 — SMTO couldn't finish reading or writing a file

GUID: c98c79d7-0f9a-4ce3-b7f9-90b016bbbc50
Slug: file-io-error
Domain: FIL · Subsystem: files

What happened

  • The computer reported a problem while SMTO was working with a file but didn't say exactly what. If SMTO was adding to or changing files, part of the change may already be saved.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the file named in Technical details on the Gateway's computer and check whether SMTO's change is already partly or fully there. Adding to a file is saved piece by piece, so some of it may already be written.
  2. Make sure the drive holding that file is connected and has free space. If it is a USB drive or network share, reconnect it. This error usually comes from the drive or network share itself, not from SMTO's request.
  3. If SMTO was comparing two files, ask it to compare smaller files or just the section you care about. The comparison helper stops when the result would be too large or when it fails.
  4. Only if the change is not already there, ask SMTO in the conversation to repeat that step. Repeating a change that already happened could add the same text twice.

What success looks like

  • The step finishes and the file shows the change you expected, exactly once.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages the Gateway's computer; a repeated read or write failure can mean a failing disk or a dropped network drive. Don't delete SMTO's saved files or folders to try to clear it.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A Gateway file operation failed with an OS or worker error that has no more specific mapping: an unmapped errno, an append that made no write progress, or a diff worker that failed or returned more than 512 KiB.

What this means

  • A filesystem exception has no more specific mapping, an append made no forward write progress, or the bounded diff worker failed/returned excessive output. File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.

Why this can happen

  • A filesystem exception has no more specific mapping, an append made no forward write progress, or the bounded diff worker failed/returned excessive output.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the safe OS error or diff-worker status and original mutation facts before diagnosing disk health or replaying work.

How to fix it

  • Read errno/winerror, message, changed_paths and partial_mutation in the receipt, and check the Gateway host's system log for the underlying I/O fault (disk, network mount, filesystem errors). Confirm partial effects before repeating; for diff failures, compare smaller inputs (gateway_core/file_common.error_kind, file_mutate.write/diff).
  • Inspect target filesystem health and the safe OS diagnostic before repeating the operation.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The actual failing operation is identified and its supported bounded check succeeds.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • File and transfer receipts retain per-item execution, publication, cleanup and partial-effect facts. These explanations do not modify files, weaken path guards or replay a write; reconcile the original state before further mutation.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
